source: Parker (1989/1990) Success in Tutoring Electronic Troubleshooting (NASA CP-3059; Sherlock)
finding: Sherlock, an avionics troubleshooting tutor for F-15 test equipment, was field tested at two Air Force wings. Tutored airmen beat the control group and neared the skill of very experienced airmen.
numbers: 16 tutored airmen (mean 28 months experience), about 20 hours on the tutor; control mean 37 months, on-the-job training; expert benchmark about 114 months; gains held at six-month delayed test.
limits: Page gave a conference abstract; full statistics are in Lesgold/Gott papers, not read here. Small N. A claimed 'four years of experience' equivalence was not found in this source.
agent_relevance: Case-driven practice with coached hints can compress experience. A scaffold could mimic this by replaying worked cases with hints.

source: Parker (1989/1990) Sherlock, same report: instructional design
finding: The report is about which tutor features caused success and how they were ported from Xerox Lisp to a PC.
numbers: Port from Lisp to PC object-oriented environment; features not itemized on the page read.
limits: Abstract only; feature list not verified.
agent_relevance: Tutor features (coaching, replay of expert path) map to review and critique operators.

source: Shute (1991) review of intelligent tutor evaluations (search-result listing)
finding: Search result described a Shute review listing Sherlock among few tutors with controlled evaluations, concluding tutors speed learning without hurting final outcome.
numbers: No numbers read; PDF was scanned images and could not be extracted.
limits: Not opened; claim is from a search summary only.
agent_relevance: Treat the speed-up claim as plausible but unverified.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for Retrieval Augmented Generation in LLMs for Legal QA
finding: Putting the retrieved full case (question plus answer) into the prompt beat the no-retrieval baseline. Hybrid embeddings worked best.
numbers: 32 test cases; Mistral-7B; cosine to reference: no-RAG 0.8967, best hybrid AnglE-BERT k=3 full case 0.9141 (about 1.94% gain); k=3 beat no-RAG at 95% confidence, one-tailed t-test.
quote: All hybrid variants performed better than the No-RAG baseline
limits: Tiny test set (32). Gain is small because no-RAG is already high from parametric memory. Metric is embedding similarity, not correctness.
agent_relevance: Case retrieval gains are small when the model already knows the domain. Use a library where the model lacks knowledge.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Automatic Root Cause Analysis via LLMs for Cloud Incidents (RCACopilot)
finding: Matching incidents to handlers, summarising diagnostics, then retrieving similar past incidents with chain-of-thought gave far better root-cause labels than plain GPT-4 prompting, GPT embedding, or fine-tuning.
numbers: Micro-F1 / Macro-F1: RCACopilot GPT-4 0.766/0.533; GPT-3.5 0.761/0.505; GPT-4 embedding 0.257/0.122; fine-tuned GPT 0.103/0.144; GPT-4 prompt only 0.026/0.004; FastText 0.076/0.004; XGBoost 0.022/0.009. One year of Microsoft email-service incidents.
limits: Single company data. Table row labels were read from scrambled PDF layout, so the row-to-method mapping is my best reading.
agent_relevance: Case memory works when the case is distilled into a summary. Raw dumps failed. Plan a fallback for new cases.

source: Chen et al. (2023) RCACopilot: handler design and unseen causes
finding: Diagnostic information is collected by expert-built decision-tree handlers (stored troubleshooting guides) per alert type, not by the model.
numbers: Handler component in use at Microsoft over four years; 163 of 653 incidents (about 25%) had a root cause not seen before.
agent_relevance: Fixed evidence-gathering steps before reasoning can play the handler role in a schema.

source: Ahmed et al. (2023) Recommending Root-Cause and Mitigation Steps for Cloud Incidents using LLMs
finding: Fine-tuned GPT-3.x models on past incidents were compared with encoder baselines. Code-davinci-002 was best among GPT models. Multi-task training helped a little.
numbers: Over 40,000 incidents, 1000+ services. Root-cause top-1 BLEU-4: RoBERTa 4.21, Davinci-002 4.24; ROUGE-L 11.43 vs 12.83 for RoBERTa. Multi-task +2.8% BLEU-4, +2.0% ROUGE-L on average.
limits: Absolute scores are low; lexical metrics. RoBERTa beat GPT on some metrics, so the win is not uniform.
agent_relevance: Learning from incident history without a case index gives weak absolute scores.

source: Ahmed et al. (2023), human validation
finding: Incident owners rated model suggestions as moderately correct and more readable than correct.
numbers: Mean correctness for Davinci and Code-davinci-002: root cause 2.88 and 2.56; mitigation 3.04 and 3.16 (scale 1-5). Readability means 2.52 to 4.08. Small rater group.
limits: Owners worried a wrong suggestion would slow on-call engineers.
agent_relevance: Fluent output can hide wrong diagnosis. Keep verification states.

source: Guan, Xu, Rogers (2026) Leveraging Resolved Incident History for LLM-Assisted Software Bug Diagnosis (OM-RAG)
finding: Indexing resolved issues as symptom-root cause-resolution triples beat chunked retrieval and a documentation graph.
numbers: 1,172 issues, LLM-judged; manual check on 123. Diagnosis accuracy: OM-RAG 0.931, chunk retrieval 0.325 (OM-RAG +186%), no retrieval 0.238 (+291%); OM-RAG +77% over documentation graph. Fix correctness 0.809. Cross-judge Spearman 0.943.
limits: One production system (Dataverse); LLM judge; authors built the system.
agent_relevance: Structure of the case record matters more than amount of text. Store cases as symptom, cause, fix triples.

source: Guan et al. (2026) OM-RAG: groundedness vs accuracy
finding: Chunk retrieval had the highest groundedness yet low accuracy: the model faithfully used the wrong kind of text.
numbers: C-chunk groundedness 0.865 but diagnosis accuracy 0.325; mean retrieval similarity of OM-RAG 0.880.
agent_relevance: A faithful answer is not a correct answer. Checks should test the cause, not only source use.

source: Wang, Yu et al. (2026) Cloud-OpsBench: Reproducible Benchmark for Agentic RCA
finding: Eleven LLMs under a ReAct loop on 754 cases across 57 fault types. Many correct diagnoses lacked complete evidence.
numbers: Mean joint RCA accuracy 0.59 (OnlineBoutique) and 0.49 (TrainTicket); best 0.78 and 0.68. GPT-5 correct but evidence-incomplete in 33.1% and 29.4% of cases.
agent_relevance: Score the evidence trail, not only the label.

source: Cloud-OpsBench audit of incomplete investigations
finding: Of audited right-answer cases with incomplete evidence, 95% were incomplete investigations; most stopped at the first symptom log.
numbers: 73% stopped at symptom log without source tracing; 22% inconclusive guessing; 5% valid alternative path. Qwen3-8B 15.78 steps with ECR 0.19; GPT-5 5.56 steps with ECR 0.39.
agent_relevance: Premature closure is the main failure. Add a forced trace-to-source step before closing.

source: Cloud-OpsBench RQ3: trajectory-as-ICL case reuse
finding: Retrieving three successful past trajectories (matched by symptom) helped on OnlineBoutique but was mixed on TrainTicket.
numbers: OnlineBoutique avg JRA 0.70 to 0.79, ECR 0.62 to 0.75. TrainTicket avg JRA 0.58 to 0.56, ECR 0.40 to 0.46. DeepSeek-V4-Flash TrainTicket JRA 0.63 to 0.55 (ICL hurt). Gemini-2.5-Flash TrainTicket ECR 0.30 to 0.48.
limits: Pool of GPT-5 successful trajectories only; 1:1 split; 3 models.
agent_relevance: Similar symptoms can have different causes, so a wrong case misleads. Cases can hurt; gate them.

source: Cloud-OpsBench RQ3: SOP (runbook) distillation
finding: Distilled category-level runbooks gave smaller and less reliable gains than raw trajectories.
numbers: OnlineBoutique avg JRA 0.71, ECR 0.64. Qwen3.5-27B JRA 0.70 to 0.63, ECR 0.61 to 0.57. TrainTicket avg JRA 0.60, ECR 0.42. Gemini SOP JRA 0.61 vs ICL 0.58 but ECR 0.39 vs 0.48.
agent_relevance: More accurate labels and more complete evidence can come from different aids.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: A case bank with a learned case-selection policy raised deep-research agent scores with no weight update.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%; DeepResearcher 66.6% F1 / 80.4% PM; case memory +4.7 to +9.6 points on out-of-distribution sets. HLE avg F1/PM 22.2/17.4 without CBR to 26.7/24.4 with; SimpleQA 81.0/89.7 to 84.7/95.0.
limits: Planner and tools differ from our setting; high tool cost.
agent_relevance: Direct support for a case library as memory.

source: Memento ablation on number of retrieved cases
finding: Retrieving four cases was best; more did not help.
numbers: K in 0,2,4,8,16,32 on DeepResearcher: best at K=4, F1 64.5, PM 78.5; flat or slightly worse above.
quote: CBR benefits from a small, high-quality memory
agent_relevance: Keep few high-quality cases (about 4), unlike few-shot where more helps.

source: Zhao et al. (2023/2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Storing past trajectories and distilling insights both help, in different tasks.
numbers: Insights-only vs retrieval-only success: HotpotQA 36%/31%, ALFWorld 50%/55%, WebShop 37%/38%. Transfer HotpotQA to FEVER: ReAct 58%, ExpeL transfer 70%.
agent_relevance: Mix general rules with concrete cases: rules for reasoning-heavy tasks, cases for action-heavy tasks.

source: ExpeL ablations
finding: Learned insights beat human-written insights. Adding reflections to insight extraction hurt. Choosing examples by task similarity beat random choice.
numbers: HotpotQA ExpeL 39.0 vs hand-crafted about 32. ALFWorld example ranking: random 40.0, reasoning-similarity 42.5, task similarity 59.0. With Reflexion rounds on ALFWorld: ExpeL 54.5 (R0) to 64.2 (R3) vs retrieve-only 40.3 to 54.4.
limits: Numbers read from layout-scrambled PDF text; some column alignment is my best reading.
agent_relevance: Case ranking by task similarity matters a lot; poor retrieval cost about 17-19 points.

source: ExpeL: experience diversity
finding: Insights drawn only from the few-shot examples gave no gain over ReAct. Success and failure pairs gathered with Reflexion beat ReAct-only data.
numbers: Extra autonomously collected experiences were essential.
agent_relevance: A case library needs failures as well as successes.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Verbal self-reflection stored in memory over repeated trials improved success without weight updates.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%; +22% absolute on AlfWorld over 12 iterations, +20% HotPotQA, +11% HumanEval.
agent_relevance: A reflection store is a case library of one's own failures.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager skill library
finding: An agent that stores verified skills as code and retrieves them for new tasks progressed far faster in Minecraft.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distance, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA; random curriculum -93% items; removing self-verification -73%.
limits: Single game; code skills are exact, unlike diagnostic cases.
agent_relevance: Verifying before storing, and ordering the curriculum, both matter for case libraries.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory (AWM)
finding: Inducing reusable workflows from past runs raised web-agent success and generalised across tasks.
numbers: WebArena +12.0 absolute points, 51.1% relative over BrowserGym; +7.6% relative over human-written-workflow SteP; Mind2Web +24.6% relative step success; cross-task gains 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test gap widens; workflow coverage 0.40 on Mind2Web test.
agent_relevance: Abstracted procedures from cases transfer better than raw cases when tasks differ.

source: Wang et al. (2024; v3 2026) Tutor CoPilot
finding: An LLM that gives novice tutors expert-style suggestions in real time raised student mastery in a randomized trial.
numbers: 700+ tutors, 1,000+ students; +4 percentage points topic mastery (p<.01); +9 points for lower-rated tutors; about $20 per tutor per year; 350,000+ messages: more probing questions, less generic praise.
limits: Math remediation, one platform; tutors kept control.
agent_relevance: Expert-thinking models plus a human in the loop work. Expert moves can be encoded as prompts.

source: Wang et al. Tutor CoPilot: how expertise was encoded
finding: Prompts were built from decomposed expert reasoning, examples of student mistakes, and sample responses; model told not to give away answers.
numbers: Gains were largest for lower-rated tutors.
agent_relevance: Decomposed expert reasoning in the prompt is a transferable method.

source: Cloud-OpsBench harness comparison
finding: With GLM-5.1 fixed, different agent architectures reached similar accuracy but different evidence closure and token cost.
numbers: Accuracy similar; closure and token cost differed substantially.
agent_relevance: Scaffold effects show in process quality, not only label accuracy.

source: Wei and Fink (2026) AgentRCA: zero-shot evidence-grounded RCA
finding: A zero-shot LLM agent with a digital twin and tool calls, no case library, was competitive with supervised baselines on two industrial facilities.
numbers: Evaluated on a multiphase-flow facility and a chemical plant; exact scores not extracted.
agent_relevance: Alternative to a case library when labelled faults are scarce.

source: BattFailScholar battery failure retrieval (press release via search)
finding: Press release says retrieval from a past-failure knowledge base raised LLM diagnosis accuracy.
numbers: Average accuracy gain 19.7% reported.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence; verify before use.

source: Cloud-OpsBench base per-model results
finding: Base ReAct performance varied by model and system.
numbers: OnlineBoutique base JRA: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0.76, Gemini-2.5-Flash 0.65, Qwen3.5-27B 0.70. TrainTicket: 0.63, 0.53, 0.58.
agent_relevance: Case retrieval helped weaker or mid models more than the strongest.
